draft.title: Synthesis, decomposition and combustion
card: two or more substances join to form one product. For example, hydrogen and oxygen form water.
one substance breaks apart into two or more simpler substances. For example, calcium carbonate breaks into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide when heated.
a fuel burns in oxygen and releases energy as heat and light. Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives carbon dioxide and water.
Synthesis and decomposition are opposites. Many reactions can be sorted by counting how many reactants and products there are.
draft.remember: Synthesis builds one product from many. Decomposition splits one reactant into many. Combustion burns a fuel in oxygen.

a.q: Which equation shows a decomposition reaction?
a.why: One reactant, hydrogen peroxide, breaks into two simpler products. The magnesium and ammonia equations join substances, so they are synthesis. The methane equation has two reactants and is combustion.
a.clue: Look for one reactant on the left.

b.q: Propane (C3H8) burns in a plentiful supply of oxygen in a camping stove. Which products form?
b.why: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in plenty of oxygen gives carbon dioxide and water. Carbon and hydrogen would mean the fuel simply broke apart, which is not burning in oxygen.
b.clue: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon has two familiar products.
